title: Saraam and the Cat Kings
summary: The Bagheera tale of their own beginning.

claims.text: Bagheera tell of Saraam, a woman who took two cat kings as mates, a black one of wisdom and magic and a spotted one of anger and war, and bore ten children, half human and half cat.
In the tale, the Moon touched each child and turned it into its opposite, and the children went out to drive the serpents from the land.
The Bagheera call their duty dhamma: keeping the truce between big cats and humans and hunting the serpent of corruption.

title: The Bagheera
summary: The werepanthers and wereleopards of India and Africa.

claims.text: Werepanthers and wereleopards are one tribe from India and northern Africa, keeping a pact begun in the Impergium under which humans and big cats keep peace with each other.
Over the ages the Bagheera pressed their Garou cousins to end the Impergium and sought peace with the Silent Striders, Children of Gaia and Black Furies.
Most Bagheera stay close to both human and feline Kin, and no other Bastet tribe is as numerous or as respected.

title: The Yava
summary: The three secrets each Bastet tribe guards.

claims.text: Bastet say their tongue, Khwar, comes from the first talks of the First Pride, and only a werecat taught by a mentor, a kuasha, grasps its finer points.
At the end of the First Year the kuasha gives the young cat three tribal secrets, the Yava, and departs; any or all of them may be true, and an outsider who learns them endangers the whole tribe.
By Seline's decree a Yava passes only with consent and no mind magic can take it, though torture can; some say early Garou tortured captive werecats for them and used them to slaughter tribes.
A kit judged unready is left alone and watched from afar, and is told the Yava only after growing up.

title: Pryio and Breeds
summary: How werecats sort themselves by birth and by the hour.

claims.text: Werecats name breeds bluntly: the human-born are monkeychildren, metis come of a forbidden union of two Bastet, and the cat-born are wildcats, raised by big cats whose numbers are dwindling.
Each Bastet also has a pryio, the time of day tied to temperament: Daylight for an open heart, Twilight for complex and artistic minds, Night for those who guard their privacy.
